# Copy and microcopy (CP)

This is the short form. Before writing code in this area, read the full rules with reasons, bad/good examples and checks: `.ui-polish/rules/14-copy.md`.

- **CP-01 No lorem ipsum** (error). Never leave lorem ipsum or any other dummy Latin in source. Where final copy is not available, write realistic draft copy for this product and mark it in your report to the owner as draft; a plausible sentence can be reviewed, placeholder Latin can only be replaced.
- **CP-02 No filler names, labels or sample data** (warning). Do not ship "Your Company", "Feature One", "Card title", "Text goes here", "John Doe", "Acme Inc", "test@test.com" or bracketed stand-ins like "[Your tagline]". Sample and seed data should look like the product's real data: varied names from more than one culture, plausible amounts, dates relative to today, statuses in realistic proportions, a couple of edge cases (a very long name, an overdue item).
- **CP-03 No vague messages** (info). Replace "Click here", "Submit", "OK", "Something went wrong", "An error occurred", "Invalid input", "No data", "Oops!" with text that names the thing. Links describe their destination ("Read the API docs"); messages name the object and the state ("No invoices match 'north'").
- **CP-04 Buttons say what they do** (warning). Button labels are a verb plus the object, in sentence case, one to three words: "Create project", "Send invoice", "Delete 3 files". The label on a confirmation dialog's primary button repeats the action ("Delete project"), never "Yes" / "OK"; the secondary is "Cancel". A button that opens further steps ends with an ellipsis only if more input is required ("Export…"). Keep the same verb for the same action everywhere (not "Remove" here and "Delete" there for the same thing).
- **CP-05 Errors say what happened and what to do** (error). An error message has two parts: what went wrong, in the user's terms, and the next step. No error codes, stack traces, or raw server messages as the main text (a code may follow in small print for support). Do not blame the user ("You entered an invalid…"); do not apologise at length. Field errors state the requirement ("Use at least 12 characters"), not the failure ("Password invalid").
- **CP-06 Empty states teach** (warning). An empty state's title says what is missing ("No invoices yet"); the description says what the area is for or why it is empty, in one sentence; the button is the action that fills it. For filtered-empty, echo the query and offer to clear it ("No clients match 'zx'. Clear search"). Avoid jokes and exclamation marks unless `design.md` sets a playful voice.
- **CP-07 Consistent voice, case and formats** (warning). Use sentence case for headings, buttons, labels and menu items (capitalise the first word and proper nouns only). One term per concept across the product (workspace or team, not both). Address the user as "you"; the product as "we" sparingly. No exclamation marks in routine UI. Numbers, currency, dates and times are formatted with `Intl` for the user's locale, with relative time for recent events ("4 minutes ago") and absolute dates on hover or for older ones. Use real typographic characters: curly quotes and apostrophes, an ellipsis character, a multiplication sign for dimensions.
